s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of sharp precordial pain with persistent symptoms and abnormal cardiac sounds
salient_findings: Sporadic clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge
Normal lung and heart auscultation except for intermittent clicking
key_facts: 19-year-old man with no past medical history
Three-week history of persistent sharp precordial pain
Pain began during an episode of gastroenteritis
Gastrointestinal symptoms resolved while chest pain remained
Pain worsened on inspiration
Clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge
Normal vital signs
Normal lung and heart auscultation except for clicking
Normal laboratory studies, including arterial blood gas, complete blood count, and cardiac troponins
Normal chest radiograph
Normal electrocardiography

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Persistent sharp precordial pain and abnormal cardiac sounds

shortlist.label: Mitral valve prolapse
shortlist.why_kept: Clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge

shortlist.label: Costochondritis
shortlist.why_kept: Pain worsened on inspiration and normal laboratory studies

shortlist.label: Precordial catch syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Sharp precordial pain and normal vital signs

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of sharp precordial pain that worsens on inspiration and the presence of a clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge are consistent with costochondritis, which is an inflammation of the cartilage that connects the ribs to the breastbone. The normal laboratory studies and electrocardiography also support this diagnosis as costochondritis is often not associated with abnormal lab results or ECG changes.

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: Pericarditis typically presents with diffuse chest pain that may improve with sitting up and leaning forward, and is often associated with abnormal ECG changes, such as widespread ST elevation, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Mitral valve prolapse
rejected.why: Mitral valve prolapse is characterized by a mid-systolic click and a late systolic murmur, which are not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Tietze syndrome
rejected.why: Tietze syndrome is similar to costochondritis but typically involves swelling of the affected area, which is not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Precordial catch syndrome
rejected.why: Precordial catch syndrome is characterized by sharp, stabbing chest pain that is typically brief and intermittent, whereas the patient's pain has been persistent for three weeks.
